title: Markdown Header Chunker
prompt:
Split a Markdown document into smaller pieces without losing which section each piece belongs to.

Implement `chunk_markdown(markdown, max_chars) -> list[str]`. Return chunks in document order; each string can contain multiple lines and must have Python `len()` at most `max_chars`.

If a section continues in a new chunk, repeat its parent headings and current heading, one per line, then a blank line before the body. For example, text under `# Guide` / `## Install` needs both headings. After `## Usage`, use Guide / Usage instead. Repeated headings and newlines count toward the limit.

For this exercise:
- Recognize `#` through `######` headings; ignore them inside code fences delimited by lines starting with triple backticks.
- Prefer splitting between paragraphs (blank lines). If a paragraph or line cannot fit, split by character budget, repeating its headings on every continuation.
- Normalize CRLF and CR to LF before splitting.
- Raise an error if `max_chars <= 0` or required headings plus their separator leave no room for body text. `assert` is allowed.

example.input:
markdown = """# Guide

## Install

First paragraph.

Second paragraph."""
max_chars = 40
example.output:
[
    """# Guide

## Install

First paragraph.""",
    """# Guide
## Install

Second paragraph."""
]
example.reasoning: Two chunks, each 37 characters including newlines. Each list element is one multiline string. The second repeats # Guide and ## Install so its paragraph keeps the same section context.
